entries.title: Nahum 1:1
segments:
vv 1-8. 
 
The glorious attributes of Jehovah make the prosperity of the righteous and the overthrow of the wicked alike certain.  He is omniscient, and no sin can escape his knowledge; he is omnipotent, and able to punish sinners however high may be their rank and power; he is infinite in righteousness, and must be the everlasting enemy of all unrightousness; he is infinite in goodness and truth, and cannot fail to be in the side of those who love him and trust in him; he is the governor and judge of the universe which he has created, and must see that obedience is rewarded and sin punished.

entries.title: Nahum 1:2
segments: God is jealous; the prophet begins with describing God's awful attributes of righteousness and omnipotent power, because it is from these that the destruction of Nineveh comes.

entries.title: Nahum 1:4
segments: Bashan--Carmel--Lebanon; the prophet's familiar reference to these places indicates clearly that Palestine was his home.

entries.title: Nahum 1:8
segments: The place thereof; literally, "her place;" that is, the place of Nineveh.

entries.title: Nahum 1:9
segments:
What do ye imagine; what is this evil device which ye are purposing? 
 
  Against the Lord; they opposed Jehovah in assaulting his people, and so Rabshakeh himself understood it.

An utter end; of Nineveh. 
 
  Shall not rise up the second time; the destruction of Nineveh shall be so complete that it shall not need to be repeated. 
 
vv 9-14. 
 
Often in the history of this world have vast empires arisen under the control of wicked men, which threatened to destroy God's church; but his has always stood by her, and suffered her persecutors to proceed only so far as was needful for her chastisement; and then he has overthrown them by the hand of other and mightier nations.

entries.title: Nahum 1:10
segments: Folden together as thorns--drunken; sunk in vice and sensuality, they are as a mass of thorns twisted together, or a heap of dry stubble, ready fuel for the fire of God's wrath.

entries.title: Nahum 1:11
segments: There is one come out; Sennacherib, who here represents the power and malice of Assyria.

entries.title: Nahum 1:12
segments:
Quiet; literally, "whole;" that is, in a prosperous and uninjured state. 
 
  Thus shall they be cut down; cut down in the midst of their prosperity. 
 
  Thee; Judah.

entries.title: Nahum 1:14
segments: Concerning thee; concerning the Assyrian.  In the original, Judah and the Assyrian are distinguished by a difference in gender; the former being feminine, the latter masculine.

entries.title: Nahum 1:15
segments:
Bringeth good tidings; of the overthrow of the Assyrian. 
 
In times of trouble let God's people be steadfast in faith; at the appointed time the glad tidings of deliverance will come, filling their hearts with gladness and their lips with praise.
